title: Manipur Minister Admits Security Lapses After Kamjong Raid
excerpt: Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam visits torched border villages as 21 remain missing after May 7 militant attack
body:
Manipur Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam visited the scorched villages of Namlee, Wanglee and Choro in Kamjong district on May 10, days after suspected Myanmar-based militants launched a pre-dawn raid that left at least 21 people missing and dozens of homes in ashes.

**What happened in Kamjong:**
Suspected militants linked to the Kuki National Army-Burma (KNA-B) carried out coordinated drone-assisted attacks on Namlee Market and Choro village in the early hours of May 7, 2026, striking around 2 AM. Around 300 armed militants reportedly crossed into Indian territory from Myanmar near Border Pillars 5 to 10 and launched assaults on villages along the frontier. Empty shells and live rounds of M16, AK-47, and LMG ammunition were found at the attack sites, underlining the seriousness of the incident.

**Security failure draws sharp scrutiny:**
Speaking to the press, Konthoujam said the government is taking the incident very seriously and that any possible security lapses would be thoroughly examined. The Home Minister stopped short of labelling the assault 'foreign aggression,' a term local legislators had already applied. Phungyar MLA Leishiyo Keishing alleged that despite the presence of a nearby police outpost under Kasom Police Station and an Assam Rifles camp located around three kilometres away, no security personnel responded during the attack. Tangkhul Naga organisations alleged the attack took place shortly after visits by Central Security Forces to the border villages, and raised concern over possible intelligence leakage and the failure of nearby security personnel to intervene effectively.

**Broader context of a volatile border:**
Manipur has remained affected by ethnic violence between the Meitei and Kuki communities since May 2023, a conflict that has claimed at least 260 lives and displaced thousands of people. More than 1,000 Myanmar nationals are presently taking shelter in different parts of Kamjong district after crossing into border areas amid instability in the neighbouring country.

**What to watch:**
Opposition leader Okram Ibobi Singh has warned that the Kamjong incident could be repeated in other parts of the state if New Delhi and Imphal do not jointly deploy adequate forces and close the intelligence gaps that allowed this raid to succeed.
nri_angle: With many Indian-Americans tracing roots to Manipur and Northeast India, the Kamjong attack signals a dangerous escalation at India's eastern frontier that directly threatens the communities they still call home.
author: Diaspora Desk
